plainText:
The Pokémon Center lady (Japanese: Pokémon Center lady), also known as the Pokémon Center Nurse or receptionist (Japanese: reception lady), is an operator of a Pokémon Center. They facilitate the restoration of s' to full HP, and usually provide this basic service free of charge.

In , they can be battled at the Battle Tree and Battle Royal Dome under the Pokémon Center Lady (Japanese: PC Lady).

In , they are referred to as the Pokémon Center clerk, and in addition to healing Pokémon, they sell items commonly sold at Poké Marts in other games. They can also be battled during the Z-A Royale under the Pokémon Center Clerk (Japanese: ポケセン受付嬢 Pokémon Center Receptionist).

Among fans, the Pokémon Center lady is often mistaken for her counterpart introduced in Pokémon the Series, Nurse Joy.

==In the core series==
 
 
A Pokémon Center lady operates every Pokémon Center in the Pokémon games (except the one in Po Town, which was taken by Team Skull), usually standing behind the counter and beside a machine which is able to heal the 's Pokémon to full health.

===Generation I===
In , their appearance was changed to simultaneously reflect the artwork and resemble Nurse Joy as she appears in Kanto, the latter which was reinforced in . They are also all accompanied by like Nurse Joy.

===Generation II===
In the , the lady at the Pokémon Center in Silent Hill is unable to heal the player's Pokémon due to ongoing maintenance.

In , the lady in Fuchsia City has green hair instead of red.

===Generation IV===
In , a lady named (Japanese: Medi) participates in Master Rank s with a Chansey nicknamed Pinky (Japanese: Chansey).

===Generation V===
In , the player's used to be a Pokémon Center lady, outright stated by her during a Xtransceiver conversation. She has mentioned working at Nimbasa City and is implied to have worked at Mistralton City. 

===Generation VI===
In , there is an old lady on Mt. Chimney that states she used to be a "Pokémon Center girl". 

===Generation VII===
In , Pokémon Center ladies named (Japanese: Ma'i) and (Japanese: Kamaloli) appear as Trainers that the player can battle in the Battle Royal Dome and Battle Tree respectively. They don't specialize in any specific type, but they have a preference for pink Pokémon and those with support capabilities. They keep their Pokémon in Heal Balls. In Ultra Sun and Ultra Moon, the player can customize to wear a Pokémon Center Nurse outfit. This outfit can be obtained from the Game Freak offices in Heahea City after the credits.

===Generation VIII===
In , although there are no Pokémon Centers, Pesselle highly resembles the Pokémon Center lady and serves as the Captain of the Galaxy Team's Medical Corps.

===Generation IX===
In , the Pokémon Center lady in Mossui Town in Kitakami has a different design and dialogue from those in Paldea. She both speaks and dresses more informally and holds a Rotom Phone that she looks at when the player is not near her. If the player joins her behind the counter and talks to her, she will refuse to heal their Pokémon, telling them to talk to her from the other side of the counter. In the Mochi Mayhem epilogue, she is the only citizen of Mossui Town not afflicted by Binding Mochi and has unique dialogue if spoken to at this point, warning the player of the strange occurrences in the town. Blueberry Academy, on the other hand, has no Pokémon Centers or Pokémon Center ladies to attend them. Instead, there are self-service healing machines located across the Terarium for students, including the player, to use.

In , the Pokémon Center clerks of Lumiose City sell items in addition to healing Pokémon, offering goods such as Poké Balls and Potions like the Poké Mart in previous games. They also have a variety of different physical appearances, with distinct facial features and skin tones. A Pokémon Center clerk operates a traveling Pokémon Center stand on the north side of Rouge Plaza, though she does not sell items. Early in the game, the lady operating the Vert District Pokémon Center installs the Pokédex app on the player's Rotom Phone.

===Pokémon===
 
 
A Pokémon Center lady named Casey competes with her , nicknamed Pinky, in and Pokémon Super Contests.

===Quotes===
 

==In the side games==
=== and ===
Pokémon Center ladies attend the Pokémon Centers of Orre, acting in the same capacity they do in the Generation III core series games. In addition, a Pokémon Center lady attends every checkpoint of the Mt. Battle challenge.

==In the spin-off games==
===Pokémon Masters EX===
The Pokémon Center of Pasio's Centra City is attended by Trista, Tricia, and Trinnia. While none of the three ladies heal the player's Pokémon directly (as they are healed automatically after completion of a given stage), they can assist the player in managing their teams, scouting new sync pairs, and accessing story content.

=== Pokémon Pokopia ===
Pokémon Center ladies are the subject of the Human Record "Career Monthly (Vol. 111)", which can be randomly found on Dream Islands. Reading this record rewards with the "Pokémon Center" outfit styled after the ladies' own outfits, which comprises of a Top, Pants, Hat and Sandals.

==In animation==

In and related media, the I Choose You! trilogy, and , most Pokémon Centers are run by characters named Nurse Joy (Japanese: Joy, referred to as Joy- by most characters). 

===Pokémon the Series===
==== ====
In Real Life...Inquire Within!, and substituted for Melemele Island's Nurse Joy as part of a work experience program. During this, versions of the uniform intended for male operators were shown, and were worn by , , and (after clearing a misunderstanding) Ash as well. The male uniform appeared again in Alola, Alola!, worn by while he helped an ailing as part of his training.

===Pokémon Horizons: The Series===
 
====Mollie====
In , Mollie resembles a Pokémon Center lady, particularly those in Alola, and originally assisted in Pokémon Centers and trained to become a , before deciding she wanted to travel and help wild Pokémon in need. Like Nurse Joy, she owns a . In The Pokémon Center Lady, it's revealed that Mollie's mother is an elderly Nurse Joy.

====Other====
In Tinkatink's Hammer Wasn't Made in a Day, a Pokémon Center lady from Kitakami was seen at Mossui Town. She does not bear a resemblance to Nurse Joy and instead resembles the Mossui Town Pokémon Center lady from The Teal Mask. She approached Mollie after seeing her performing medical procedures on the Countryside Harvest Festival participants. After exchanging a few words, the Pokémon Center lady injured her tooth with one of Murdock's caramel apples. She reappeared in a flashback in Mochi Mayhem!.

=====Voice actors=====
 

===Pokémon Origins===
Pokémon Center ladies made a couple of appearances during Pokémon Origins, serving the same role as in the games. The first one was seen in Viridian City in File 1: Red, while another one appeared in Lavender Town in File 2: Cubone. Unlike in most other media, these ladies are different from each other, having different appearances and voices.

===Pokémon Generations===
Two Pokémon Center ladies from Lumiose City made a brief cameo appearance in the Pokémon Generations episode The Beauty Eternal, where they were seen during a televised interview with Lysandre. Similar to Pokémon Origins, they have unique designs that differ from one another.

===Pokémon Evolutions===
A Pokémon Center lady appeared in a cameo in the Pokémon Evolutions episode The Champion. Her outfit and appearance is the same as the Pokémon Center ladies in .

Pokémon Center Evolutions.png|A Pokémon Center lady in Pokémon Evolutions
 

==In the manga==
 ]]
===The Electric Tale of Pikachu===
In addition to Nurse Joy, several generic Pokémon Center ladies appear in The Electric Tale of Pikachu, first appearing in Clefairy Tale. They appear in a wide variety of outfits, which vary from city to city.

===Pokémon Adventures===
In Wartortle Wars, a Pokémon Center lady at the Celadon City Pokémon Center healed 's Pika while Red received a call from .

In Pinsir Changes, a Pokémon Center lady at the Anistar City Pokémon Center was tied up as Essentia disguised as her to steal 's Xerneas. Her appearance was based on the Pokémon Center lady within the Generation VI games.

===Pokémon Gold & Silver: The Golden Boys===
A Pokémon Center lady appeared in A Promise Given to Miltank.
 

==In the TCG==
A called appears in the . The art on this card slightly resembles Nurse Joy from the , but has blue hair. The nurse appearing on the card also seems to have been based on the games.

A second card, titled , debuted in the expansion, both as a regular print and a . Both have illustrations of Pokémon Center ladies from Generation VI.
